### Replace `apps/api/test/integration/test-env.ts` (whole file)

```ts
import { existsSync, readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
import { parseEnv } from "node:util";

const ENV_FILE = fileURLToPath(new URL("../../.env.test", import.meta.url));
/** 3f: the watcher's role is the fourth, so that no test of the watcher can write into the development database. */
const DATABASE_KEYS = ["DATABASE_URL_API", "DATABASE_URL_AUTH", "DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE", "DATABASE_URL_NOTIFY"] as const;

/** The Redis database the integration tests own. Development uses database 0. */
export const TEST_REDIS_DATABASE = 15;

/** The integration test environment: apps/api/.env.test, which scripts/gen-dev-env.mjs derives from apps/api/.env. */
export function loadTestEnv(file: string = ENV_FILE): Record<string, string> {
  if (!existsSync(file)) {
    throw new Error("apps/api/.env.test is missing. Run `node scripts/gen-dev-env.mjs`, then `node scripts/test-db.mjs`.");
  }
  const parsed = parseEnv(readFileSync(file, "utf8"));
  return Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(parsed).filter((entry): entry is [string, string] => typeof entry[1] === "string"));
}

/**
 * The integration run truncates every table and flushes its Redis database, so it must never point
 * at development data. Messages name the key and the database, never the URL, which holds a password.
 */
export function assertTestTargets(env: Record<string, string | undefined>): void {
  for (const key of DATABASE_KEYS) {
    const value = env[key];
    if (!value) throw new Error(`Refusing to run integration tests: ${key} is not set.`);
    const database = decodeURIComponent(new URL(value).pathname.replace(/^\//, ""));
    if (!database.endsWith("_test")) {
      throw new Error(`Refusing to run integration tests: ${key} points at database "${database}", not at a database whose name ends in _test. Run \`node scripts/gen-dev-env.mjs\`.`);
    }
  }
  const redis = env.REDIS_URL;
  if (!redis) throw new Error("Refusing to run integration tests: REDIS_URL is not set.");
  const index = new URL(redis).pathname.replace(/^\//, "") || "0";
  if (index !== String(TEST_REDIS_DATABASE)) {
    throw new Error(`Refusing to run integration tests: REDIS_URL selects database "${index}", not ${TEST_REDIS_DATABASE}. Run \`node scripts/gen-dev-env.mjs\`.`);
  }
}
```

### Replace `apps/api/test/lab/README.md` (whole file)

```markdown
# The contention lab of moderation decisions

`contention.lab.ts` measures what a decision's transaction costs and what it meets (3c design, sections 2 and 12),
against the test database with migration 0016. The design names no place for it; it lives here.

It is a database lab. It issues its statements itself, as SQL: a decision is the lock on its subject's profile row, its
row in `decisions` and its rows in `decision_actions`, whose triggers do the rest; a like, a follow, the author's
deletion and the purge are the statements the social and media repositories issue; the purge's delete is the ordered
delete by owner (`delete from post_media where id in (select id from post_media where owner_id = $1 order by id for
update) returning id`). An intake is the moderation module's `recordIntake`. It uses no code of a later task.

Every measured transaction is rolled back, so the lab leaves no decision, and writes no audit row but one: the R4
removal that the redaction's rounds need committed (the last section) is a real, confirmed decision. The accounts it commits
(the large ones, written in bulk by the migrator, and the pair for the two-session rounds) are removed when it ends.

## Running it

From `apps/api`, with the scratch stack's data services up and the test database migrated:

    node ../../node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --config vitest.lab.config.ts

No suite includes it (its file ends in `.lab.ts`). It takes three to four minutes. Each measurement is one line of JSON
in `.data/lab-contention.jsonl` at the repository's root (or the file `LAB_OUT` names), with `busyPercent`: the share of
processor time, over all cores, that was not idle in the second and a half before the measurement.

## The numbers of 2026-10-04, first run: a saturated machine

PostgreSQL 18 in the scratch stack's container on a Windows machine shared with other work. The machine was saturated
throughout: `busyPercent` read 94 to 99 before every measurement, most of it other projects' containers. These numbers
are upper bounds for this hardware; the second run below, on a quieter machine, is the one the design asks for.

### An account's seal (one session; one image on each post)

| image posts | busy | decision row | seal taken while deciding | answer that ends it | seal for good | lifting it |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1,000 | 97% | 104 ms | 180 ms | 254 ms | 282 ms | 232 ms |
| 5,000 | 99% | 18 ms | 1,123 ms | 1,057 ms | 1,131 ms | 995 ms |

- The seal taken while deciding locks the account's image rows in id order, writes one row of `seal_posts` for each post
  and writes every image row once. At 5,000 image posts the decision and its seal take 1.1 s, 0.19% of the ten minutes a
  step-up challenge lives.
- The seal for good that follows writes every image row twice in one transaction: the answer ends the first seal (each
  row back to visible, 1.06 s at 5,000), and the new seal seals each again (1.13 s). Lifting it is a fourth write (1.0 s).
- No post row is locked by any of them.

### The purge of an account (one session)

| image rows | frozen | busy | tombstones | ordered delete | rows deleted | whole purge |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5,000 | no | 99% | 436 ms | 2,228 ms | 5,000 | 2.7 s |
| 5,000 | yes | 98% | 390 ms | 1,862 ms | 0 | 2.3 s |
| 20,000 | no | 94% | 1,471 ms | 6,090 ms | 20,000 | 7.6 s |
| 20,000 | yes | 97% | 1,724 ms | 5,821 ms | 0 | 7.6 s |

- The keep trigger reads the freeze once for each row: about 0.3 to 0.45 ms a row under this load, whether the row is
  then kept or deleted. The research lab's figures under load were 2 to 4 s at 5,000 rows and 7 to 16 s at 20,000; these
  lie at their lower end.
- "Frozen" is an unanswered report of child sexual abuse material about the account: every row is kept, and the delete
  answers none.

### A decision against everything else (two sessions, 40 rounds a pair, each side first in half of them)

Three decisions (an interim withhold of a post; a final removal that closes the post's case; a seal on the author's
account's case followed in the same transaction by the answer that ends it) against six other transactions (a like of
the post; a follow of the author; the author's deletion of the post; the author's purge; a notice of child sexual abuse
material that names the post and its author's account; a report of the post under a rule). Each side holds its locks for
15 ms before it rolls back. `busyPercent` was 96.

| decision | against | both completed | deadlocks | lock timeouts | longest transaction |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| interim withhold | like | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 236 ms |
| interim withhold | follow | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 116 ms |
| interim withhold | author's deletion | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 158 ms |
| interim withhold | purge | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 232 ms |
| interim withhold | notice naming post and account | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 409 ms |
| interim withhold | report under a rule | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 318 ms |
| closing removal | like | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 183 ms |
| closing removal | follow | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 145 ms |
| closing removal | author's deletion | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 194 ms |
| closing removal | purge | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 171 ms |
| closing removal | notice naming post and account | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 207 ms |
| closing removal | report under a rule | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 231 ms |
| account's seal and its answer | like | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 254 ms |
| account's seal and its answer | follow | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 210 ms |
| account's seal and its answer | author's deletion | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 233 ms |
| account's seal and its answer | purge | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 419 ms |
| account's seal and its answer | notice naming post and account | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 264 ms |
| account's seal and its answer | report under a rule | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 206 ms |

- 720 rounds, no deadlock and no lock timeout. The purge met none here either: the deadlock the design expects of it is
  with an intake that locks the account's image rows, which the intake does not do before Task 3.
- What makes this hold: a decision takes its subject's profile row first, as the author's deletion and the purge do; a
  like and a follow take that row in a mode a decision's does not conflict with; a seal locks image rows only; and an
  intake takes its cases in one order and each post's row only to read it.
- A finding the lab led to, now a test (`moderation-races.test.ts`): a report that arrives while a decision is closing
  its target's case waits where it opens a case (`insert into cases ... on conflict do nothing` waits for the transaction
  that is changing the conflicting row), and then opens a new case without a retry. The retry on `case_closed` is needed
  only when the decision has locked the case and not yet closed it when the report reads it.

## The numbers of 2026-10-04, second run: the final migration, a quieter machine

Run again after the review added a second deferred check to 0016 (queued by every row of the ledger, it runs at COMMIT,
which the lab's rolled-back transactions never reach). `busyPercent` read 17 to 28.

| image posts | busy | decision row | seal taken while deciding | answer that ends it | seal for good | lifting it |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1,000 | 19% | 35 ms | 70 ms | 115 ms | 110 ms | 107 ms |
| 5,000 | 17% | 7 ms | 420 ms | 463 ms | 503 ms | 465 ms |

At 5,000 image posts the seal taken while deciding takes 0.43 s with its decision, 0.07% of the challenge's ten minutes;
the seal for good that follows it writes every image row twice in under a second.

| image rows | frozen | busy | tombstones | ordered delete | rows deleted | whole purge |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5,000 | no | 28% | 182 ms | 888 ms | 5,000 | 1.1 s |
| 5,000 | yes | 24% | 108 ms | 791 ms | 0 | 0.9 s |
| 20,000 | no | 22% | 680 ms | 2,488 ms | 20,000 | 3.2 s |
| 20,000 | yes | 27% | 576 ms | 2,366 ms | 0 | 2.9 s |

The keep trigger costs about 0.12 to 0.18 ms a row here.

The two-session rounds at 24% busy: the same 18 pairs of 40 rounds each, every transaction completed, no deadlock and no
lock timeout, the longest transaction 124 ms.

# The lab of the intake's lock statement

`hold.lab.ts` measures what an intake's hold costs and what it meets (3c design, sections 5 and 12, Task 3), at the
repository: `MediaForCases.hold` with an owner pair, which is the statement that locks every image row on an account's
posts when a report of child sexual abuse material names the account
(`select ... from post_media m join posts p on p.id = m.post_id where m.post_id = any($1) or m.owner_id = any($2) order
by m.id for key share of m`). It also times the disposal's two statements over the same accounts, and runs the purge
against a notice about a post that quotes its author's own post. It runs against the test database with migration 0016,
through the media repository and the moderation module's own `recordIntake`; the purge is the social repository's
`purgeProfile` with the media repository's `purgeOwner` as its last act. Every measured transaction is rolled back; the
accounts it commits are removed when it ends.

    node ../../node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --config vitest.lab.config.ts test/lab/hold.lab.ts

It takes about a minute and a quarter. Each measurement is one line of JSON in `.data/lab-hold.jsonl` (or the file
`LAB_OUT` names), with `busyPercent` as above. `LAB_ROUNDS` sets how many rounds the two sessions meet by chance (40
unless said).

## The numbers of 2026-10-04

Three runs on the shared Windows machine, PostgreSQL 18 in the scratch stack's container: two before the review of
Task 3 and one after its fixes. The machine was never quiet, most of the load other projects' containers:
`busyPercent` read 14 to 40 before the lock statement's runs of the first run (up to 100 before its last measurements),
14 to 83 before those of the second and 15 to 40 throughout the third. The times are upper bounds.

### The lock statement (`hold` with one owner pair; one image on each post; three runs each, a transaction of its own each)

| attached rows | run | busy | lock statement | WAL written |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5,000 | first | 29 to 40% | 36, 25 and 21 ms | 288, 274 and 274 kB |
| 5,000 | second | 64 to 83% | 90, 65 and 26 ms | 288, 274 and 274 kB |
| 5,000 | third | 23 to 31% | 46, 31 and 28 ms | 288, 274 and 274 kB |
| 20,000 | first | 14 to 19% | 114, 80 and 69 ms | 1,153, 1,097 and 1,097 kB |
| 20,000 | second | 14 to 76% | 102, 180 and 198 ms | 1,408, 1,097 and 1,097 kB |
| 20,000 | third | 23 to 31% | 151, 123 and 102 ms | 1,153, 1,097 and 1,097 kB |

- The research lab's figures (`lab-gate-k`, H) were 77 ms and 287 kB at 5,000 rows and 102 ms and 1.1 MB at 20,000:
  these agree. The lock writes its mark to each row it takes, though no column changes: about 55 bytes of WAL a row.
- The plan is LockRows over a Sort on `m.id` over a hash join of `post_media` and `posts`, as the design says of the
  owner form. In the test database the lab's account owns most image rows, so `post_media` is scanned whole; the sort
  took 0.6 MB of memory at 5,000 rows and 2.5 MB at 20,000.
- A whole notice on the path for child sexual abuse material that names the account (its rows, the copy of the profile,
  the hold and the snapshot) took 72, 95 and 77 ms at 5,000 rows and 104, 238 and 147 ms at 20,000; one that names a
  post of the account as well took 85, 91 and 80 ms at 5,000 and 743 (at 90% busy), 299 and 147 ms at 20,000.
- The purge's ordered delete (`purgeOwner`) right after such a notice, in the same transaction, deleted no row: 1.4,
  1.6 and 1.3 s at 5,000 rows, 5.6 and 5.5 s (73 to 100% busy) and 3.2 s (31% busy) at 20,000, the keep trigger reading
  the freeze once for each row.

### The disposal's two statements (one batch of `dropDisposable`, and `overdueDeletions`)

The account's rows are all attached. In the first two lines nothing of the account is disposable: its posts are
visible. In the last, the account is reported on the path for child sexual abuse material and every post of it is
deleted, so every row carries a mark of disposal and none may go.

| what | attached rows | busy | `dropDisposable` | `overdueDeletions` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| nothing disposable, the freeze a condition of its own (as first built) | 5,000 | 100% | 3,332 ms | 3,332 ms |
| | 20,000 | 97% | 14,226 ms | 13,863 ms |
| nothing disposable, the marks tested first (as built now) | 5,000 | 24% | 18 ms | 8 ms |
| | 20,000 | 40% | 62 ms | 19 ms |
| every row marked and frozen (as built now) | 5,000 | 18% | 1,285 ms | 1,174 ms |
| | 20,000 | 26% | 4,148 ms | 3,666 ms |

- As first built, the predicate was `... and (marks) and (m.post_id is null or not public.post_frozen(m.post_id))`.
  The second condition names `post_media` alone, so the planner made it the filter of that table's scan and called the
  freeze for every attached image row in the table before a mark was tested. The review measured 0.9 s at 5,000 rows
  and 3.4 s at 20,000 on a quieter machine; the first two lines are the same statement on a saturated one.
- Now the marks and the freeze are one condition, `case when (marks) then (m.post_id is null or not
  public.post_frozen(m.post_id)) else false end`: it names all three tables, so it runs where they are joined, and the
  freeze is read only for a row that carries a mark. `media-cases.test.ts` pins that no scan's filter names the
  predicate, under the planner's own plan and under each join method alone.
- What remains is the last pair of lines: a frozen account whose posts are all deleted (a purged account under an
  unanswered report, or under a seal for good) costs one read of the freeze for each kept row, about 0.2 ms, at every
  round of the disposal and at every count of overdue rows, for as long as the freeze lasts.

### The purge against a notice about a post that quotes its author's own post

A report of child sexual abuse material about a post that quotes another is taken in as two items, so a notice about a
post that quotes its author's own post holds two posts of one account for share, in id order, while the purge writes
both. The lab's account has such a pair, four images on each post; the notice names the quoting post and the account.
The notice's side counts the runs the moderation module made, so a deadlock it absorbed by running again shows; nothing
runs a purge again, so a deadlock that picks the purge shows as its error.

By chance (two sessions, each side first in half the rounds, a few milliseconds ahead, each holding its locks for
15 ms before it rolls back):

| purge | rounds | busy | purge | notice | deadlocks | longest transaction |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| as first built (counters, then the posts in id order) | 200 | 95% | 200 of 200 | 200 of 200, each in one run | 0 | 528 ms |
| as built now (every post locked first, in id order) | 40 | 25% | 40 of 40 | 40 of 40, each in one run | 0 | 139 ms |

Staged (ten rounds a shape: the notice has copied the first of the two posts and is held there, the purge comes to
wait, the notice goes on to the second post):

| purge | the quoting post has the lower id | the quoted post has the lower id and was deleted by its author |
|---|---|---|
| as first built: the counters of what its posts quote, then the posts in id order | 10 of 10: the purge ends with 40P01 | not run |
| the account's posts that are not deleted locked first, in id order | 10 of 10: both complete | 10 of 10: the purge ends with 40P01 |
| every post of the account locked first, in id order (as built now) | 10 of 10: both complete | 10 of 10: both complete |

- As first built, the purge's quote counter wrote the quoted post before the ordered statement asked for the quoting
  one, which the notice held: each waited for the other. The window is one statement of the notice wide, so 200 rounds
  by chance never met it, and every staged round did. PostgreSQL ended the purge each time: a session looks for a
  deadlock once it has waited a second, and the purge was the first to wait. The notice went through in one run. A purge
  that ends this way is finished by the purge job within five minutes.
- Locking only the posts that are not deleted leaves the same wait in the second shape: a live post that quotes (or
  replies to) its author's own deleted post has that post's counter written by the purge, and a report of child sexual
  abuse material holds a deleted post like any other. So the purge locks every post of the account first.
- What stays unordered: the counters of other accounts' posts that the purged account replied to, quoted, liked or
  reposted, which the purge writes after its own posts; and the author's deletion of one post, which writes the post
  and then the post it replied to or quoted.
- Before the review this pair ran with two plain posts (and with the purge as first built): 40 of 40 on both sides in
  both runs, no deadlock, the longest transaction 307 ms at 64% busy and 200 ms at 23%.
- What the two-session tests add (`media-cases.test.ts`): when the notice locks first, the purge waits and then keeps
  every attached row; when the purge deletes first, the notice waits, locks nothing and is stored without an error.

### The contention lab again

`contention.lab.ts` issues the purge's statements as the repositories issue them since Task 3: every post of the
account locked in id order (`select id from posts where author_id = $1 order by id for update`), then the tombstones,
and the ordered delete of the image rows last. Three runs on 2026-10-04 with the intake locking image rows and placing
its holds. The first, before the review, still tombstoned by one ordered statement and met a machine at 9 to 14% busy
(53 and 93 before the two purges of 20,000 rows). The second and the third issue the statements above: the second met
a saturated machine (93 to 100% throughout), so its times say more about the machine than about the change; the third
a quiet one (6 to 16%). "Tombstones" is the lock statement and the update together.

| image rows | frozen | run | busy | tombstones | ordered delete | rows deleted | whole purge |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5,000 | no | first | 9% | 170 ms | 891 ms | 5,000 | 1.1 s |
| 5,000 | yes | first | 14% | 120 ms | 827 ms | 0 | 1.0 s |
| 20,000 | no | first | 53% | 603 ms | 4,019 ms | 20,000 | 4.6 s |
| 20,000 | yes | first | 93% | 1,440 ms | 4,249 ms | 0 | 5.7 s |
| 5,000 | no | second | 100% | 481 ms | 3,136 ms | 5,000 | 3.6 s |
| 5,000 | yes | second | 100% | 309 ms | 3,423 ms | 0 | 3.8 s |
| 20,000 | no | second | 100% | 1,934 ms | 8,112 ms | 20,000 | 10.1 s |
| 20,000 | yes | second | 100% | 2,249 ms | 8,467 ms | 0 | 10.7 s |
| 5,000 | no | third | 16% | 91 ms | 827 ms | 5,000 | 0.9 s |
| 5,000 | yes | third | 6% | 103 ms | 730 ms | 0 | 0.8 s |
| 20,000 | no | third | 13% | 442 ms | 2,207 ms | 20,000 | 2.7 s |
| 20,000 | yes | third | 13% | 481 ms | 1,977 ms | 0 | 2.5 s |

Locking the posts first costs nothing that shows: at 5,000 posts the lock statement and the update together took 91
and 103 ms, where the one ordered statement took 170 and 120 ms.

The 18 pairs of 40 rounds: in every run each transaction completed, with no deadlock and no lock timeout; the longest
transaction was 137 ms in the first (12% busy), 562 ms in the second (100% busy) and 116 ms in the third (13% busy).
The account's seal taken while deciding: 84 ms at 1,000 image posts and 2.2 s at 5,000 in the first run (13% busy; 0.4
and 1.1 s in Task 2's runs), 361 ms and 3.3 s in the second, 58 and 156 ms in the third.

### What the lab's tests found

- **A batch that was not one.** `dropDisposable` as the design writes it (`delete from post_media where id in (select
  ... order by id limit $1 for update)`) can delete more than its limit. When the planner joins the delete's rows to
  the sub-select by a nested loop, the sub-select runs again for every row; each run skips the rows this statement has
  deleted already and lets the next ones in. On a fresh test database one call deleted all 60 disposable rows under a
  limit of 25, and with hash joins, merge joins, materialising, hashed aggregation and sorting switched off it deleted
  33 of 36. The repository therefore chooses the batch in a materialized common table expression, which runs once
  whatever the plan (`with batch as materialized (select ... order by m.id limit $1 for update of m) delete from
  post_media where id in (select id from batch) returning id`); `media-cases.test.ts` holds the bound under those
  planner settings. The ordered deletes of the author's deletion and the purge have no limit, so the same re-run changes
  nothing they delete.
- **The freeze read for every row.** The disposal's two statements, above.
- **The purge and its own posts.** The staged rounds, above.

## The numbers of 2026-10-09: the R4 redaction (migration 0018)

`contention.lab.ts` gains one test for `redact_r4_body` (3c design, sections 2 and 6.4): the redaction takes its
decision's case, then the post, then the post's images in id order, the order of `moderation_apply` and of an intake's
locks, and the design asks for it to be measured against both. The post has four images. Its R4 removal is the one
thing this lab confirms with a real staff key (the software authenticator, as `decideForTest` does), because a
redaction acts only on a committed decision; it is dated back seven months, so that it is final for its author. The
redaction itself, and everything that runs against it, is rolled back in every round, so each round finds the decision
due again. The removal's case goes with the lab's accounts at the end; its one audit row stays, as every real
decision's does. Run alone with `-t "the R4 redaction"`.

Two runs: the test alone on a machine busy with other work (`busyPercent` 82), then the whole file on a quieter one
(`busyPercent` 22; the whole file took 122 s).

| the redaction against | rounds | redaction | other side | longest transaction, busy | longest, quieter |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| (alone, one session) | 1 | ok | | 67 ms | 29 ms |
| an interim withhold on the post's other, open case, whose trigger runs `moderation_apply` on the post | 40 | 40 ok | 40 ok | 233 ms | 68 ms |
| a report under a rule, which locks the post `FOR SHARE` and holds its images | 40 | 40 ok | 40 ok | 125 ms | 104 ms |
| a notice of child sexual abuse material naming the post and its author's account, which locks the images through both | 40 | 40 ok | 40 ok | 123 ms | 83 ms |

- No deadlock and no refusal in 120 rounds of either run, each side first in half of them. The redaction and a decision on the post's
  other case meet at the post's row, which both take `FOR UPDATE` before any image row; the redaction and a report meet
  there too (`FOR UPDATE` against `FOR SHARE`); a notice that reaches the images through the account takes them
  `FOR KEY SHARE`, which the redaction's `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` does not wait for.
- That last pair is the one the design accepts as a race and not as a wait (6.4): a report about the author's account
  that commits between the redaction's check of the freeze and its erasure of the snapshots leaves the body blank, the
  snapshots kept and the decision unmarked, and the round after the answer finishes it. The database test of
  `redact_r4_body` stages exactly that.

## orders/: the lab of authorities' orders (sub-project 3f)

`orders/` is the lab the 3f design rests on (its section 3, LAB A to F), copied here unchanged but for its line ends from
`korbat-scratch/research-3e/lab-3f/`, which lies outside the repository: `RUN.txt` holds every command and the machine it
ran on, `make_proto.py` and `20-tables.sql` the prototype of the design's sections 6.2 and 6.3, `21-helpers.sql` the
API's statements, the lettered SQL files the labs themselves, and `out-*.txt` their raw outputs. It ran on a throwaway
cluster of PostgreSQL 18.1 over the migrations 0000 to 0016. The task that builds the ledger's migration of 3f runs it
again on the 18.6 image, as `RUN.txt` lists it, and compares the outputs.
```

### Replace `apps/api/test/mail/moderation-templates.test.ts` (whole file)

```ts
import { describe, expect, test } from "vitest";
import { ACCOUNT_ITEM_SCOPE, ACCOUNT_SUSPECT_SCOPE, ALERT_KINDS, ALREADY_NOT_SHOWN, QUOTE_ITEM_SCOPE, REPLY_AIM_HOURS, STANDING_RULES, SUSPECT_OUTCOME_PHRASES, UNSEEN_NO_ACTION, isTimeFact, outcomeWords, renderAlert, type AlertKind } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { noticeTime } from "../../src/auth/flows/notify";
import type { MailMessage, NoticeUpdateData, NoticeUpdateLine, TemplateName } from "../../src/mail/mailer";
import { MemoryMailer } from "../../src/mail/memory";
import { DECISION_MAIL_SUBJECTS, renderMail, renderNoticeUpdate, renderTemplate } from "../../src/mail/templates";

/**
 * The mails of deciding and of the dispatch (3c design, section 7.15): the author's statement, the staff alerts for a
 * burst of decisions, for a decision that lifted the protection of reported images and for cases that wait too long, and
 * the one structured mail, the daily update of decisions on a person's reports. Each is pinned word for word.
 */
const LAST_USER = "korbat staff never ask for your password or a code, and korbat does not read replies to this email.";
const LAST_STAFF = "korbat never puts a link in a staff email.";
const paragraphs = (text: string) => text.trimEnd().split("\n\n");
const TIME = "2026-10-04 06:59 UTC";

/** No link of any kind, and the staff mails' last sentence. */
function linkless(r: { text: string; html: string }) {
  expect(r.text).not.toMatch(/https?:|www[.]|:[/][/]/);
  expect(r.html).not.toMatch(/<img|<a |href=|https?:/);
  expect(paragraphs(r.text).at(-1)).toBe(LAST_STAFF);
}

describe("the closed union of templates", () => {
  test("holds 46 templates: the 25 before moderation cases, the nine of 3c, the two of 3e's Task 3, the three of its Task 4, the two of its Task 5 and the five staff mails of 3f's Task 1", () => {
    // Every name is written out: a template added or dropped changes this list.
    const names = [
      "sign_in_code", "sign_up_code", "reauth_code", "new_device", "account_locked", "mfa_enabled", "mfa_disabled", "password_changed", "recovery_codes_regenerated", "sessions_revoked_all",
      "email_change_code", "email_changed", "email_change_reverted", "badge_verified", "badge_removed", "delete_account_code", "account_deleted", "passkey_added", "passkey_removed", "passkey_suspect",
      "recovery_code_used", "staff_key_added", "staff_session_started", "staff_key_suspect", "staff_keys_revoked",
      "notice_received", "notice_update", "moderation_decision", "moderation_urgent", "moderation_waiting", "moderation_burst", "moderation_reads", "moderation_reveal", "moderation_csam_lifted",
      "suspension_started_at_once", "suspension_lifted",

    ] as const satisfies readonly TemplateName[];
    expect(new Set(names).size).toBe(46);
    // Each name is a template the union holds, and the union holds no other: the assignment below would not compile.

    expect(Object.keys(all)).toHaveLength(46);

describe("moderation_decision: the statement of reasons, to its author", () => {
  const statement = ["korbat removed your post of 2026-10-01 12:00 UTC: other people can no longer see it.", "The facts: The post offers followers for money.", "You can appeal this decision once."].join("\n");

  test("the subject follows the decision's kind and outcome, from one table", () => {
    expect(DECISION_MAIL_SUBJECTS).toEqual({
      seal_deciding: "korbat sealed images of yours while it decides",
      seal_final: "korbat sealed images of yours",
      post_deciding: "A post of yours is under review on korbat",
      profile_deciding: "korbat reset part of your profile while it decides",
      post_restricted: "korbat restricted a post of yours",
      profile_restricted: "korbat restricted part of your profile",
      lifted_deciding: "korbat lifted a restriction it placed while deciding",
      reversed: "korbat reversed a decision about your account",
      appeal_kept: "korbat answered your appeal",
    });
    for (const [key, subject] of Object.entries(DECISION_MAIL_SUBJECTS)) expect(renderTemplate("moderation_decision", { subject: key, statement }).subject, key).toBe(subject);
    // A subject that is no key of the table is a programming error, never printed as given.
    expect(() => renderTemplate("moderation_decision", { subject: "Click here to appeal", statement })).toThrow(/subject/);
  });

  test("the statement's paragraphs, one per line of the data, then where to read it, and that no korbat mail carries a link to act on a decision", () => {
    const r = renderTemplate("moderation_decision", { subject: "post_restricted", statement });
    expect(paragraphs(r.text)).toEqual([
      "korbat removed your post of 2026-10-01 12:00 UTC: other people can no longer see it.",
      "The facts: The post offers followers for money.",
      "You can appeal this decision once.",
      "Read it in korbat under Settings, Cases. korbat's emails never contain a link to act on a decision.",
      LAST_USER,
    ]);
    expect(r.text).not.toMatch(/https?:|:[/][/]/);
    expect(r.html).not.toMatch(/<img|<a |href=/);
    // A staff text is only ever text: what it holds never becomes markup, and an empty line is no paragraph.
    const hostile = renderTemplate("moderation_decision", { subject: "post_restricted", statement: "The facts: <script>alert(1)</script>\n\nkorbat's reasons: <b>x</b>" });
    expect(hostile.html).toContain("&lt;script&gt;alert(1)&lt;/script&gt;");
    expect(hostile.html).not.toMatch(/<script|<b>/);
    expect(paragraphs(hostile.text)).toHaveLength(4);
    expect(() => renderTemplate("moderation_decision", { subject: "post_restricted" })).toThrow(/statement/);
    expect(() => renderTemplate("moderation_decision", { statement })).toThrow(/subject/);
  });
});

    // 3e: the replies to a suspension or a termination unanswered for longer than korbat's aim, after the lanes and the measures.
    const replies = renderTemplate("moderation_waiting", { lane1Count: "1", lane1Oldest: TIME, replyCount: "2", replyOldest: TIME });
    expect(paragraphs(replies.text)).toEqual([
      `Lane 1: 1 case waiting longer than 24 hours, since ${TIME}.`,
      `2 replies to a suspension or termination have waited more than ${REPLY_AIM_HOURS} hours, the oldest since ${TIME}. A reply sent before the start holds its suspension until someone answers.`,
      "Open the staff console. The same reminder went to every staff phone.",
      LAST_STAFF,
    ]);
    linkless(replies);
    expect(paragraphs(renderTemplate("moderation_waiting", { replyCount: "1", replyOldest: TIME }).text)[0]).toBe(
      `1 reply to a suspension or termination has waited more than ${REPLY_AIM_HOURS} hours, since ${TIME}. A reply sent before the start holds its suspension until someone answers.`,
    );
    expect(() => renderTemplate("moderation_waiting", { replyCount: "2" })).toThrow(/replyOldest/);
    // A count without its time, and a mail about nothing, are programming errors.
    expect(() => renderTemplate("moderation_waiting", { lane0Count: "2" })).toThrow(/lane0Oldest/);
    expect(() => renderTemplate("moderation_waiting", {})).toThrow(/nothing/);
  });
});

describe("notice_update: decisions on a person's reports, once a day", () => {
  const POST = "http://localhost:8081/post/0190f3a2-7c1e-7b1a-9f00-0123456789ab";
  const PAGE = "http://localhost:8081/notice/N-ABCDEFGH23#t=AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA";
  const TERMS = "http://localhost:8081/terms";
  const COURTS = "go to court, or complain to the Digital Services Coordinator of the EU country where you live (Article 53 of the Digital Services Act).";
  const REEXAMINE = "You can ask korbat once, within six months and free of charge, to re-examine a moderator's decision to take no action: it is decided again as a new report.";
  const FINAL = "A decision changed on review or by a correction, or given on re-examination, is final within korbat.";
  const line = (more: Partial<NoticeUpdateLine> = {}): NoticeUpdateLine => ({
    ref: "N-ABCDEFGH23",
    item: 1,
    link: POST,
    outcome: outcomeWords({ outcome: "restricted_legal", rule: null, suspect: false, sealed: false, unseen: false, noEffect: false, scope: null }),
    reexamination: false,
    changed: false,
    reexaminable: false,
    unseen: false,
    automatic: false,
    ...more,
  });
  const noAction = outcomeWords({ outcome: "no_violation", rule: null, suspect: false, sealed: false, unseen: false, noEffect: false, scope: null });
  const update = (more: Partial<NoticeUpdateData>): NoticeUpdateData => ({ signedIn: false, lines: [], receipts: [], pages: [], ...more });

  test("signed out: one paragraph per line, the page of each notice it has a line for, that nothing was automated, and the courts", () => {
    const r = renderNoticeUpdate(update({ lines: [line(), line({ item: 2, link: "http://localhost:8081/u/ada" })], pages: [{ ref: "N-ABCDEFGH23", pageUrl: PAGE }] }));
    expect(r.subject).toBe("Decisions on your reports to korbat");
    expect(paragraphs(r.text)).toEqual([
      `N-ABCDEFGH23, item 1 (${POST}): access restricted: korbat found it illegal.`,
      "N-ABCDEFGH23, item 2 (http://localhost:8081/u/ada): access restricted: korbat found it illegal.",
      `To see report N-ABCDEFGH23 or ask for a re-examination of a decision on it, open this page: ${PAGE}`,
      "No automated means were used to decide.",
      `You can ${COURTS}`,
      LAST_USER,
    ]);
    // The page link stands at the end of its paragraph, and nothing is an anchor.
    expect(r.text).toMatch(/#t=A{43}$/m);
    expect(r.html).not.toMatch(/<img|<a |href=/);
  });

  test("signed in: no page link, and the re-examination points to Your reports", () => {
    const r = renderNoticeUpdate(update({ signedIn: true, lines: [line({ outcome: noAction, reexaminable: true })] }));
    expect(paragraphs(r.text)).toEqual([
      `N-ABCDEFGH23, item 1 (${POST}): no action: korbat found no breach of its rules and nothing illegal.`,
      "No automated means were used to decide.",
      `${REEXAMINE} Use korbat's Settings, Cases, Your reports.`,
      `You can also ${COURTS}`,
      LAST_USER,
    ]);
    expect(r.text).not.toMatch(/[/]notice[/]|#t=/);
    // A signed-in update never carries a page or a receipt: handed either, it is refused rather than mailed.
    expect(() => renderNoticeUpdate(update({ signedIn: true, lines: [line()], pages: [{ ref: "N-ABCDEFGH23", pageUrl: PAGE }] }))).toThrow(/signed-in/);
  });

  test("the re-examination sentence goes only with a re-examinable line, and points to the page when signed out", () => {
    const withIt = renderNoticeUpdate(update({ lines: [line({ outcome: noAction, reexaminable: true })], pages: [{ ref: "N-ABCDEFGH23", pageUrl: PAGE }] }));
    expect(paragraphs(withIt.text)).toContain(`${REEXAMINE} Use the page linked in this email for that report.`);
    expect(paragraphs(withIt.text)).toContain(`You can also ${COURTS}`);
    const without = renderNoticeUpdate(update({ lines: [line()] }));
    expect(without.text).not.toContain("re-examine a moderator's decision");
    expect(paragraphs(without.text)).toContain(`You can ${COURTS}`);
  });

  test("a re-examination's answer and a changed outcome are final within korbat; a line that reads UNSEEN_NO_ACTION never is, re-examined again or not", () => {
    const answered = renderNoticeUpdate(update({ lines: [line({ outcome: noAction, reexamination: true })] }));
    expect(paragraphs(answered.text)[0]).toBe(`N-ABCDEFGH23, item 1 (${POST}), re-examined: no action: korbat found no breach of its rules and nothing illegal.`);
    expect(paragraphs(answered.text)).toContain(FINAL);
    expect(answered.text).not.toContain("re-examine a moderator's decision");
    const changed = renderNoticeUpdate(update({ lines: [line({ outcome: "korbat reversed its decision to restrict it.", changed: true })] }));
    expect(paragraphs(changed.text)).toContain(FINAL);
    // An answer given while nobody could open the images does not spend the re-examination, also when it answered one.
    const unseenLine = { outcome: UNSEEN_NO_ACTION, unseen: true };
    const open = renderNoticeUpdate(update({ lines: [line({ ...unseenLine, reexamination: true, reexaminable: true })] }));
    expect(paragraphs(open.text)[0]).toBe(`N-ABCDEFGH23, item 1 (${POST}), re-examined: ${UNSEEN_NO_ACTION}`);
    expect(open.text).not.toContain(FINAL);
    expect(open.text).toContain(REEXAMINE);
    // Asked again before a retried mail went out: no longer re-examinable, and still not final.
    const asked = renderNoticeUpdate(update({ lines: [line({ ...unseenLine, reexamination: true, reexaminable: false })] }));
    expect(asked.text).not.toContain(FINAL);
    expect(asked.text).not.toContain(REEXAMINE);
    // A line of each kind in one update: each sentence once.
    const both = renderNoticeUpdate(update({ lines: [line({ outcome: noAction, reexaminable: true }), line({ item: 2, outcome: noAction, reexamination: true })] }));
    expect(both.text.split(FINAL).length - 1).toBe(1);
    expect(both.text.split(REEXAMINE).length - 1).toBe(1);
  });

  test("only a link that named nothing is called automatic", () => {
    const dead = outcomeWords({ outcome: "not_available", rule: null, suspect: false, sealed: false, unseen: false, noEffect: false, scope: null });
    const r = renderNoticeUpdate(update({ lines: [line(), line({ item: 2, outcome: dead, automatic: true })] }));
    expect(paragraphs(r.text)).toContain("No automated means were used to decide, except for links found to name nothing on korbat, which were checked automatically.");
    expect(paragraphs(r.text)).toContain("If a link was wrong, send a new report with the right link.");
    const live = renderNoticeUpdate(update({ lines: [line()] }));
    expect(paragraphs(live.text)).toContain("No automated means were used to decide.");
    expect(live.text).not.toContain("If a link was wrong");
  });

  test("the outcome's words are the contracts': ALREADY_NOT_SHOWN, the scopes, the sealed phrase and UNSEEN_NO_ACTION stand in a line exactly as composed, with one full stop", () => {
    const facts = { rule: null, suspect: false, sealed: false, unseen: false, noEffect: false, scope: null } as const;
    const outcomes = [
      outcomeWords({ ...facts, outcome: "restricted_legal", noEffect: true }),
      outcomeWords({ ...facts, outcome: "no_violation", scope: "account" }),
      outcomeWords({ ...facts, outcome: "restricted_legal", sealed: true, scope: "account_suspect" }),
      outcomeWords({ ...facts, outcome: "no_violation", scope: "quote" }),
      outcomeWords({ ...facts, outcome: "no_violation", unseen: true }),
    ];
    const r = renderNoticeUpdate(update({ lines: outcomes.map((outcome, index) => line({ item: index + 1, outcome })) }));
    const lines = paragraphs(r.text).slice(0, outcomes.length);
    outcomes.forEach((outcome, index) => expect(lines[index]).toBe(`N-ABCDEFGH23, item ${index + 1} (${POST}): ${outcome}`));
    for (const sentence of [ALREADY_NOT_SHOWN, ACCOUNT_ITEM_SCOPE, ACCOUNT_SUSPECT_SCOPE, QUOTE_ITEM_SCOPE, SUSPECT_OUTCOME_PHRASES.sealed, UNSEEN_NO_ACTION]) expect(r.text).toContain(sentence);
    expect(r.text).not.toMatch(/[.][.]/);
  });

  test("a folded receipt rides in the update with its page link; an update of receipts alone has another subject and none of the decisions' sentences", () => {
    const receipt = { ref: "N-ZZZZZZZZ77", time: TIME, items: POST, pageUrl: "http://localhost:8081/notice/N-ZZZZZZZZ77#t=BBBB" };
    const alone = renderNoticeUpdate(update({ receipts: [receipt], termsUrl: TERMS }));
    expect(alone.subject).toBe("korbat received your reports");
    expect(paragraphs(alone.text)).toEqual([
      `korbat received your report N-ZZZZZZZZ77 at ${TIME}. It names: ${POST}.`,
      "To see where your report stands, ask for a re-examination of a decision, confirm that you sent it, or stop korbat's emails about reports to this address, open this page: http://localhost:8081/notice/N-ZZZZZZZZ77#t=BBBB",
      `How korbat handles reports, and what it keeps: ${TERMS}.`,
      LAST_USER,
    ]);
    // Two folds on one day and a line of another notice: the receipts first, the terms once, then the line and its page.
    const second = { ...receipt, ref: "N-YYYYYYYY66", pageUrl: "http://localhost:8081/notice/N-YYYYYYYY66#t=CCCC" };
    const full = renderNoticeUpdate(update({ receipts: [receipt, second], termsUrl: TERMS, lines: [line()], pages: [{ ref: "N-ABCDEFGH23", pageUrl: PAGE }] }));
    expect(full.subject).toBe("Decisions on your reports to korbat");
    const out = paragraphs(full.text);
    expect(out.slice(0, 5).map((paragraph) => paragraph.slice(0, 42))).toEqual([
      "korbat received your report N-ZZZZZZZZ77 a",
      "To see where your report stands, ask for a",
      "korbat received your report N-YYYYYYYY66 a",
      "To see where your report stands, ask for a",
      "How korbat handles reports, and what it ke",
    ]);
    expect(full.text.split("How korbat handles reports").length - 1).toBe(1);
    expect(out[5]).toBe(`N-ABCDEFGH23, item 1 (${POST}): access restricted: korbat found it illegal.`);
    expect(out[6]).toBe(`To see report N-ABCDEFGH23 or ask for a re-examination of a decision on it, open this page: ${PAGE}`);
    // A receipt needs the terms' address, and an update of nothing at all is a programming error.
    expect(() => renderNoticeUpdate(update({ receipts: [receipt] }))).toThrow(/termsUrl/);
    expect(() => renderNoticeUpdate(update({}))).toThrow(/nothing/);
  });

  test("it carries only what korbat generated: no member of the data holds a report's words", () => {
    const keys = Object.keys(line()).sort();
    expect(keys).toEqual(["automatic", "changed", "item", "link", "outcome", "reexaminable", "reexamination", "ref", "unseen"]);
  });
});

describe("the mailers take the union of messages", () => {
  test("the memory mailer renders a flat message with renderTemplate and the structured one with renderNoticeUpdate, keeps the two apart, and reads a code only from a flat message", async () => {
    const mailer = new MemoryMailer();
    const structured: MailMessage = { to: "a@b.io", template: "notice_update", data: { signedIn: true, lines: [], receipts: [], pages: [] } };
    // An update of nothing is refused as the real mailer would refuse it, before it counts as sent.
    await expect(mailer.send(structured)).rejects.toThrow(/nothing/);
    expect([mailer.sent.length, mailer.updates.length]).toEqual([0, 0]);
    await mailer.send({ to: "a@b.io", template: "sign_in_code", data: { code: "111111" } });
    await mailer.send({
      to: "a@b.io",
      template: "notice_update",
      data: { signedIn: true, lines: [{ ref: "N-ABCDEFGH23", item: 1, link: "http://localhost:8081/u/ada", outcome: "no action.", reexamination: false, changed: false, reexaminable: false, unseen: false, automatic: false }], receipts: [], pages: [] },
    });
    // The two kinds are kept apart, so a reader of the flat ones never meets a structure.
    expect(mailer.sent.map((message) => message.template)).toEqual(["sign_in_code"]);
    expect(mailer.updates.map((message) => message.template)).toEqual(["notice_update"]);
    expect(mailer.lastCodeFor("a@b.io")).toBe("111111");
    expect(renderMail(mailer.updates[0]!).subject).toBe("Decisions on your reports to korbat");
    expect(renderMail(mailer.sent[0]!).subject).toBe("Your korbat sign-in code");
  });

  test("a time in a mail is printed as noticeTime prints it", () => {
    expect(noticeTime(new Date("2026-10-04T06:59:59.999Z"))).toBe(TIME);
  });
});

describe("3e: the statement mails of a suspension taken at once and of its lift (design, sections 7.15 and 18, W.6)", () => {
  const lines = ["korbat suspended your account for 7 days, from this decision until 2026-10-11 09:30 UTC, without notice beforehand.", "The facts: The account posted a threat."];
  const statement = lines.join(String.fromCharCode(10));
  const READ = "Read it in korbat under Settings, Cases. korbat's emails never contain a link to act on a decision.";

  test("suspension_started_at_once: its subject, its lead with the days and the end, the statement's paragraphs, where to read it, and no link", () => {
    const r = renderTemplate("suspension_started_at_once", { measure: "suspend", days: "7", endsAt: "2026-10-11 09:30 UTC", statement });
    expect(r.subject).toBe("korbat suspended your account");
    expect(paragraphs(r.text)).toEqual([
      "korbat suspended your korbat account for 7 days, until 2026-10-11 09:30 UTC. It did so at once, without notice beforehand; the reasons follow. You can reply and appeal in korbat from now: sign in and use the banner on any screen.",
      ...lines,
      READ,
      LAST_USER,
    ]);
    expect(r.text).not.toMatch(/https?:|www[.]/);
    expect(paragraphs(renderTemplate("suspension_started_at_once", { measure: "suspend", days: "1", endsAt: "2026-10-05 09:30 UTC", statement }).text)[0]).toContain("for 1 day, until");
    // A termination's lead names no days and no end.
    const t = renderTemplate("suspension_started_at_once", { measure: "terminate", statement });
    expect(t.subject).toBe("korbat terminated your account");
    expect(paragraphs(t.text)[0]).toBe("korbat terminated your korbat account. It did so at once, without notice beforehand; the reasons follow. You can reply and appeal in korbat from now: sign in and use the banner on any screen.");
    expect(() => renderTemplate("suspension_started_at_once", { measure: "suspend", statement })).toThrow(/days/);
  });

  test("suspension_lifted: a lead for each state of the period, for a lift and for a basis that broke, and none says the account is free of every measure", () => {
    const lead = (why: string, period: string) => {
      const r = renderTemplate("suspension_lifted", { measure: "suspend", why, period, statement });
      expect(paragraphs(r.text).slice(1)).toEqual([...lines, READ, LAST_USER]);
      return [r.subject, paragraphs(r.text)[0]];
    };
    expect(lead("lifted", "not_started")).toEqual(["korbat lifted the suspension of your account", "korbat lifted the suspension of your korbat account that it had announced: it never starts."]);
    expect(lead("lifted", "running")).toEqual(["korbat lifted the suspension of your account", "korbat lifted the suspension of your korbat account. This suspension no longer restricts your account."]);
    expect(lead("lifted", "ended")).toEqual(["korbat lifted the suspension of your account", "korbat lifted a past suspension of your korbat account: it no longer counts toward a later suspension."]);
    expect(lead("basis", "not_started")).toEqual(["A suspension of your account will not start", "korbat reversed a decision that the suspension it announced for your korbat account rested on. The suspension will not start."]);
    expect(lead("basis", "running")).toEqual(["A suspension of your account has ended", "The suspension of your korbat account has ended, because a decision it rested on was reversed. This suspension no longer restricts your account."]);
    expect(lead("basis", "ended")).toEqual(["A past suspension of your account no longer counts", "korbat reversed a decision that a past suspension of your account rested on; that suspension no longer counts."]);
    for (const why of ["lifted", "basis"]) {
      for (const period of ["not_started", "running", "ended"]) expect(renderTemplate("suspension_lifted", { measure: "suspend", why, period, statement }).text).not.toMatch(/as before|handed to your mail provider|delivered/);
    }
    expect(renderTemplate("suspension_lifted", { measure: "terminate", why: "lifted", period: "running", statement }).subject).toBe("korbat lifted the termination of your account");
    // Task 4: a withdrawal needs the withdrawn decision's time; a why the template does not have is a programming error.
    expect(() => renderTemplate("suspension_lifted", { measure: "suspend", why: "replaced", period: "running", statement })).toThrow(/decidedAt/);
    expect(() => renderTemplate("suspension_lifted", { measure: "suspend", why: "answered", period: "running", statement })).toThrow(/why/);
  });
});

describe("3e Task 4: the mails of an announced measure, of the answer to a reply, of a withdrawal, and of a termination's take-down (design, section 18, W.6)", () => {
  const lines = ["korbat will suspend your account for 3 days. Nothing is restricted yet.", "The facts: The account had 3 active strikes."];
  const statement = lines.join(String.fromCharCode(10));
  const READ = "Read it in korbat under Settings, Cases. korbat's emails never contain a link to act on a decision.";
  const EARLIEST = "2026-10-11 09:30 UTC";

  test("suspension_announced: its subject, its lead with the days, the window and the earliest start, the reply, then the statement; a termination's without days", () => {
    const r = renderTemplate("suspension_announced", { measure: "suspend", days: "3", window: String(STANDING_RULES.replyWindowHours), earliestStart: EARLIEST, statement });
    expect(r.subject).toBe("korbat has decided to suspend your account: you can reply first");
    expect(paragraphs(r.text)).toEqual([
      `korbat has decided to suspend your korbat account for 3 days. Nothing is restricted yet. The suspension starts ${STANDING_RULES.replyWindowHours} hours after korbat sent this email, and not before ${EARLIEST}.`,
      `You can reply before it starts: sign in to korbat, where this decision is always shown and a banner on every screen gives the exact time and a Reply button. A reply sent before ${EARLIEST} is certainly in time, and holds the start until a moderator has answered you.`,
      "The decision and its reasons follow.",
      ...lines,
      READ,
      LAST_USER,
    ]);
    expect(r.text).not.toMatch(/https?:|www[.]|handed to your mail provider|delivered/);
    expect(paragraphs(renderTemplate("suspension_announced", { measure: "suspend", days: "1", window: "168", earliestStart: EARLIEST, statement }).text)[0]).toContain("for 1 day.");
    const t = renderTemplate("suspension_announced", { measure: "terminate", window: "168", earliestStart: EARLIEST, statement });
    expect(t.subject).toBe("korbat has decided to terminate your account: you can reply first");
    expect(paragraphs(t.text)[0]).toBe(`korbat has decided to terminate your korbat account. Nothing is restricted yet. The termination starts 168 hours after korbat sent this email, and not before ${EARLIEST}.`);
    expect(() => renderTemplate("suspension_announced", { measure: "suspend", window: "168", earliestStart: EARLIEST, statement })).toThrow(/days/);
    expect(() => renderTemplate("suspension_announced", { measure: "suspend", days: "3", earliestStart: EARLIEST, statement })).toThrow(/window/);
  });

  test("reply_answered: a lead for a kept and for a reversed answer, then the answer's statement", () => {
    const kept = renderTemplate("reply_answered", { outcome: "kept", statement });
    expect(kept.subject).toBe("korbat answered your reply");
    expect(paragraphs(kept.text)).toEqual(["A moderator read your reply and kept the decision. The answer and its reasons follow.", ...lines, READ, LAST_USER]);
    expect(paragraphs(renderTemplate("reply_answered", { outcome: "reversed", statement }).text)[0]).toBe("A moderator read your reply and reversed the decision. The answer follows.");
    expect(() => renderTemplate("reply_answered", { outcome: "withdrawn", statement })).toThrow(/outcome/);
  });

  test("suspension_lifted for a withdrawal: never an answer to the reply, and the sentence on the reply only when one was filed", () => {
    const r = renderTemplate("suspension_lifted", { measure: "suspend", why: "replaced", decidedAt: "2026-10-04 09:30 UTC", replied: "true", statement });
    expect(r.subject).toBe("korbat withdrew the suspension it announced");
    expect(paragraphs(r.text)).toEqual([
      "korbat withdrew the suspension of your korbat account that it announced on 2026-10-04 09:30 UTC, because it is taking another measure on your account. This is not a decision on your reply.",
      "The decision about the other measure reaches you separately.",
      ...lines,
      READ,
      LAST_USER,
    ]);
    expect(paragraphs(renderTemplate("suspension_lifted", { measure: "terminate", why: "replaced", decidedAt: "2026-10-04 09:30 UTC", replied: "false", statement }).text)[0]).toBe(
      "korbat withdrew the termination of your korbat account that it announced on 2026-10-04 09:30 UTC, because it is taking another measure on your account.",
    );
  });

  test("termination_final: the decision's day, that it is final, what is deleted, the sentence on sealed images only when images are sealed, and never that korbat keeps nothing when they are", () => {
    const r = renderTemplate("termination_final", { decided: "2026-04-04 09:30 UTC", imagesSealed: "false" });
    expect(r.subject).toBe("korbat has closed your terminated account");
    expect(paragraphs(r.text)).toEqual([
      "korbat's decision of 2026-04-04 09:30 UTC to terminate your korbat account is final: the time to appeal has passed, or your appeal was answered and the decision kept, and no reply of yours is unanswered.",
      "korbat has closed the account and is now deleting its posts and profile and every image it has not sealed, as that decision said. This cannot be undone. The handle stays reserved, so nobody else can take it.",
      "korbat keeps nothing to recognise a new account of yours by. A new account that carries on what this one was terminated for breaks korbat's terms.",
      LAST_USER,
    ]);
    const sealed = renderTemplate("termination_final", { decided: "2026-04-04 09:30 UTC", imagesSealed: "true" });
    expect(paragraphs(sealed.text)[2]).toBe(
      "korbat keeps nothing to recognise a new account of yours by. Images of yours that korbat sealed stay with it for the authorities alone, as the decision that sealed them said. A new account that carries on what this one was terminated for breaks korbat's terms.",
    );
    for (const mail of [r, sealed]) expect(mail.text).not.toMatch(/https?:|www[.]|@[a-z]/);
    expect(() => renderTemplate("termination_final", { imagesSealed: "false" })).toThrow(/decided/);
  });
});

describe("3e Task 5: the statement mails of a warning about reporting and of a restriction of it (design, sections 7.15 and 18, W.6)", () => {
  const lines = ["korbat warns you about your reports. Nothing is restricted.", "The facts: In the 90 days up to 2026-10-04 the account sent 8 reports."];
  const statement = lines.join(String.fromCharCode(10));

    expect(paragraphs(r.text)).toEqual([
      "korbat has looked at the reports your account sent under its rules and warns you about them. Nothing is restricted. The reasons, the reports concerned and what may follow are below.",
      ...lines,
      READ,
      LAST_USER,
    ]);
    expect(r.text).not.toMatch(/https?:|www[.]/);
    expect(r.html).not.toMatch(/<img|<a |href=/);
    expect(() => renderTemplate("reporting_warned", {})).toThrow(/statement/);
  });

  test("reporting_restricted: its subject, its lead with the days and the end and that illegal content can still be reported, then the statement", () => {
    const r = renderTemplate("reporting_restricted", { days: "30", endsAt: "2026-11-03 09:30 UTC", statement });
    expect(r.subject).toBe("korbat restricted your reports under its rules");
    expect(paragraphs(r.text)).toEqual([
      "korbat takes no reports under its rules from your account for 30 days, until 2026-11-03 09:30 UTC. You can still report illegal content. The reasons follow.",
      ...lines,
      READ,
      LAST_USER,
    ]);
    expect(paragraphs(renderTemplate("reporting_restricted", { days: "1", endsAt: "2026-10-05 09:30 UTC", statement }).text)[0]).toContain("for 1 day, until");
    expect(r.text).not.toMatch(/https?:|www[.]/);
    expect(() => renderTemplate("reporting_restricted", { endsAt: "2026-11-03 09:30 UTC", statement })).toThrow(/days/);
    expect(() => renderTemplate("reporting_restricted", { days: "30", statement })).toThrow(/endsAt/);
  });
});

describe("3f: the staff mails whose words are their push's (W.4)", () => {
  const NOW = "2026-10-16T09:00:00.000Z";
  /** A kind's mail as the alert tick sends it: the row's facts as text, and the time it is sent, for the day of its times. */
  const mail = (template: TemplateName, facts: Record<string, string>) => renderTemplate(template as Parameters<typeof renderTemplate>[0], { ...facts, now: NOW });

  test("each is the kind's title after korbat:, then its sentence and its line of what to do from ALERT_TEXTS, and the staff mails' last sentence", () => {
    const cases: [TemplateName, AlertKind, Record<string, string>][] = [
      ["contact_mail", "contact_mail", { receivedAt: "2026-10-16T08:05:00.000Z", dueAt: "2026-10-16T09:05:00.000Z" }],
      ["contact_mail_escalated", "contact_mail_escalated", { receivedAt: "2026-10-16T08:05:00.000Z", dueAt: "2026-10-16T09:05:00.000Z" }],
      ["order_due", "order_due", { dueAt: "2026-10-16T09:05:00.000Z", minutesLeft: "15" }],
      ["mailbox_unreachable", "mailbox_unreachable", { since: "2026-10-15T23:00:00.000Z" }],
      ["alert_channel_down", "alert_channel_down", { since: "2026-10-16T08:57:00.000Z" }],
    ];
    for (const [template, kind, facts] of cases) {
      const r = mail(template, facts);
      const counted = Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(facts).map(([name, value]) => [name, isTimeFact(name) ? value : Number(value)]));
      const text = renderAlert(kind, counted, new Date(NOW));
      expect(r.subject, template).toBe(`korbat: ${text.title}`);
      expect(paragraphs(r.text), template).toEqual([text.sentence, text.todo, LAST_STAFF]);
      linkless(r);
    }
    expect(paragraphs(mail("contact_mail", { receivedAt: "2026-10-16T08:05:00.000Z", dueAt: "2026-10-16T09:05:00.000Z" }).text)[0]).toBe(
      "Mail at the authorities' contact point, received 08:05 UTC. If it is a removal order it is due 09:05 UTC.",
    );
    expect(mail("order_due", { dueAt: "2026-10-16T09:05:00.000Z", minutesLeft: "0" }).subject).toBe("korbat: 0 minutes left");
  });

  test("they carry counts and UTC times only: a fact of another name, a time that is no time and a missing one are refused, and no handle or address is printed", () => {
    expect(() => mail("contact_mail", { receivedAt: "2026-10-16T08:05:00.000Z" })).toThrow(/dueAt/);
    expect(() => mail("mailbox_unreachable", { since: "yesterday" })).toThrow(/since/);
    expect(() => mail("alert_channel_down", { since: "2026-10-16T08:57:00.000Z", handle: "mod_anna" })).toThrow(/handle/);
    expect(() => renderTemplate("alert_channel_down", { since: "2026-10-16T08:57:00.000Z" })).toThrow(/now/);
    for (const template of ["contact_mail", "contact_mail_escalated", "order_due", "mailbox_unreachable", "alert_channel_down"] as const) {
      const facts = Object.fromEntries(ALERT_KINDS[template].facts.map((name) => [name, isTimeFact(name) ? "2026-10-16T08:00:00.000Z" : "3"]));
      expect(mail(template, facts).text, template).not.toMatch(/@/);
    }
  });
});
```

```ts
import { PgDialect } from "drizzle-orm/pg-core";
import type { SQL } from "drizzle-orm";
import pino from "pino";
import { describe, expect, test } from "vitest";
import { ALERT_KINDS } from "@korbat/contracts";
import type { AuthForModeration, StaffMessage } from "../src/auth";
import { MemoryStore, type RateLimitStore } from "../src/middleware/rate-limit";
import { URGENT_ALERT_KEY, URGENT_ALERT_WINDOW_MS, alertFacts, alertUrgentLane, staffAlert } from "../src/moderation/alerts";
import { createBackground, type ModerationDeps } from "../src/moderation/context";

/**
 * The staff alerts' throttle, their second leg and the work a request starts without waiting for it (3c design, sections
 * 7.1 step 5 and 7.12; 3f design, sections 5 and 7.2), without a database: the limit store is the in-memory one or a
 * stand-in that fails, the auth module a stand-in that takes, or does not take, the mail, and the database a stand-in
 * that records each statement. After the throttle, staffAlert writes one row of alert_outbox, which the watcher pushes,
 * then mails as 3c did; for 3c's and 3e's kinds, whose mail says more than the row's facts, it then marks the row mailed
 * whether or not an address took the mail, so the alert tick never renders such a mail from a row.
 */

const message: StaffMessage = { template: "moderation_urgent", count: 2, oldest: new Date("2026-10-04T06:59:59.123Z") };
const dialect = new PgDialect();

/** What the alert needs: a store, an auth module whose mailStaff answers as scripted, a log that keeps its warnings, and a database that records. */
function world(options: { accepted?: number[]; limits?: RateLimitStore; waiting?: { n: number; oldest: string | null }; insertFails?: boolean } = {}) {
  let now = 1_000_000;
  const store = options.limits ?? new MemoryStore(() => now);
  const mails: StaffMessage[] = [];
  const warnings: string[] = [];
  const accepted = [...(options.accepted ?? [])];
  const statements: { text: string; params: unknown[] }[] = [];
  /** The order of what happened: each row written, each mail, each row marked mailed. */
  const order: string[] = [];
  let ids = 40;
  const execute = async (statement: SQL) => {
    const q = dialect.sqlToQuery(statement);
    statements.push({ text: q.sql, params: q.params });
    if (/insert into public[.]alert_outbox/.test(q.sql)) {
      if (options.insertFails) throw new Error("the database refused the row");
      order.push(`row ${q.params[0]}`);
      return [{ id: String(++ids) }];
    }
    if (/update public[.]alert_outbox set mailed_at/.test(q.sql)) {
      order.push("marked");
      return [];
    }
    // The one read the urgent alert makes: how many cases wait in the urgent lane, and since when.
    return [options.waiting ?? { n: 2, oldest: "2026-10-04T06:59:59.123Z" }];
  };
  const deps = {
    limits: store,
    auth: {
      mailStaff: async (sent: StaffMessage) => {
        mails.push(sent);
        order.push(`mail ${sent.template}`);
        return accepted.length > 0 ? accepted.shift()! : 1;
      },
    } as unknown as AuthForModeration,
    log: { warn: (_fields: unknown, text: string) => warnings.push(text), error: (_fields: unknown, text: string) => warnings.push(text) } as unknown as ModerationDeps["log"],
    apiDb: { execute, transaction: async <T>(run: (tx: { execute: typeof execute }) => Promise<T>) => run({ execute }) } as unknown as ModerationDeps["apiDb"],
  };
  const rows = () => statements.filter((s) => /insert into public[.]alert_outbox/.test(s.text)).map((s) => s.params);
  return { deps, mails, warnings, store, statements, order, rows, advance: (ms: number) => (now += ms) };
}

  test("settle resolves once every task has ended, those started meanwhile included; a task that throws is logged and stops nothing", async () => {

    const done: string[] = [];
    let release!: () => void;
    const held = new Promise<void>((resolve) => {
      release = resolve;
    });
    background.start(async () => {
      await held;
      done.push("first");
      // A task may start another: settle waits for that one too.
      background.start(async () => {
        await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 20));
        done.push("started meanwhile");
      });
    });
    const failure = new Error("the relay fell over");
    background.start(async () => {
      throw failure;
    });
    let settled = false;
    const settling = background.settle().then(() => {
      settled = true;
    });
    await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 20));
    expect(settled).toBe(false);
    expect(errors).toEqual([failure]);
    release();
    await settling;
    expect(done).toEqual(["first", "started meanwhile"]);
    // With nothing running, settle resolves at once.
    await background.settle();
  });
});
```

```ts
import { describe, expect, test } from "vitest";
import { ModerationErrorCode } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { ModerationError, isModerationErrorCode, moderationErrorMessage } from "../src/moderation/context";

describe("the moderation module's refusals", () => {
  test("each of the thirty-two codes this module raises answers with the status the design gives it (3c design, section 10; 3e design, section 10; 3f design, section 10.6)", () => {
    const statuses = {
      notice_link_invalid: 422,
      notice_link_offsite: 422,
      human_check_failed: 403,
      staff_cannot_report: 403,
      notice_not_found: 404,
      already_reported: 409,
      appeal_not_open: 422,
      appeal_exists: 409,
      reexamination_not_open: 422,
      reexamination_exists: 409,
      case_changed: 409,
      case_closed: 409,
      staff_recused: 403,
      staff_target: 403,
      admin_required: 403,
      reviewer_conflict: 403,
      decision_cap: 429,
      profile_changed: 409,
      snapshot_mismatch: 409,
      snapshot_erased: 409,
      text_not_found: 409,
      invalid_decision: 422,
      text_invalid: 422,
      text_quotes_user: 422,
      image_refused: 404,
      reveal_refused: 422,
      // 3e (design, section 10.5).
      reporting_restricted: 403,
      reply_not_open: 422,
      strike_mismatch: 409,
      standing_conflict: 409,
      ground_not_established: 422,
      // 3f: a message at the contact point that already has its disposition.
      message_handled: 409,
    } as const;
    // The table above is the whole of the contracts' list, so a code added there fails here until its status is pinned.
    expect(Object.keys(statuses).sort()).toEqual([...ModerationErrorCode.options].sort());
    for (const [code, status] of Object.entries(statuses) as [keyof typeof statuses, number][]) {
      const err = new ModerationError(code);
      expect([err.name, err.code, err.status], code).toEqual(["ModerationError", code, status]);
      expect(err.message, code).toBe(moderationErrorMessage(code));
      expect(err.message.length, code).toBeGreaterThan(10);
      expect(isModerationErrorCode(code), code).toBe(true);
    }
    // What the audit function raises is an answer of the decision, never one of these codes.
    expect(isModerationErrorCode("staff_confirmation_ended")).toBe(false);
    expect(isModerationErrorCode("staff_confirmation_late")).toBe(false);
    // The module's own answers beside them.
    expect([new ModerationError("not_found").status, new ModerationError("invalid_request").status]).toEqual([404, 400]);
    // A session that has not finished onboarding is refused as requireSession refuses it, in the same words.
    expect(new ModerationError("onboarding_required")).toMatchObject({ status: 403, message: "Choose a handle to finish setting up your account." });
    expect([new ModerationError("rate_limited").status, new ModerationError("service_unavailable").status]).toEqual([429, 503]);
  });

  test("the console's refusals say nothing about who reported: a recusal reads the same whoever the conflict concerns, and an image that is not shown gives no reason", () => {
    expect(moderationErrorMessage("staff_recused")).not.toMatch(/report/i);
    expect(moderationErrorMessage("image_refused")).toBe("That image is not shown.");
    expect(moderationErrorMessage("reveal_refused")).not.toMatch(/@|https?:/);
  });

  test("the words of an appeal and of a re-examination are written for the person asking, and give one answer for every reason it is not open", () => {
    expect(moderationErrorMessage("appeal_not_open")).toBe("This decision cannot be appealed now.");
    expect(moderationErrorMessage("appeal_exists")).toBe("You have already appealed this decision.");
    expect(moderationErrorMessage("reexamination_not_open")).toBe("A re-examination cannot be asked for this item now.");
    expect(moderationErrorMessage("reexamination_exists")).toBe("A re-examination of this item has already been asked for.");
    // The reviewer's own refusal names their part in the case, never anyone else's.
    expect(moderationErrorMessage("reviewer_conflict")).toBe("You cannot review this appeal: you took part in its case.");
    expect(moderationErrorMessage("reviewer_conflict")).not.toMatch(/report/i);
  });

  test("the words of the notice routes are written for the person reporting, and the human check names no address", () => {
    expect(moderationErrorMessage("human_check_failed")).toBe("We could not verify that you are human. Try again.");
    expect(moderationErrorMessage("already_reported")).toBe("You already reported this; it is being looked at.");
    for (const code of ["notice_link_invalid", "notice_link_offsite", "human_check_failed", "staff_cannot_report", "notice_not_found"] as const) {
      expect(moderationErrorMessage(code), code).not.toMatch(/@|https?:/);
    }
  });
});
```

```ts
import pino from "pino";
import { afterEach, describe, expect, test, vi } from "vitest";
import { ACCOUNT_ITEM_SCOPE, ACCOUNT_MEASURE_SCOPE, ACCOUNT_SUSPECT_SCOPE, ALREADY_NOT_SHOWN, OUTCOME_PHRASES, QUOTE_ITEM_SCOPE, SUSPECT_NO_SEAL, SUSPECT_OUTCOME_PHRASES, UNSEEN_NO_ACTION } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { RULEBOOKS } from "@korbat/rules";
import type { JobLock } from "../src/lib/jobs";
import { MemoryStore } from "../src/middleware/rate-limit";
import { createModeration, type CreateModerationOptions } from "../src/moderation";
import { ALERT_TICK_INTERVAL_MS, ALERT_TICK_JOB } from "../src/moderation/alerts";
import { DISPATCH_INTERVAL_MS, DISPATCH_JOB, WAITING_ALERT_KEY, WAITING_ALERT_WINDOW_MS, stillCalls, updateLine } from "../src/moderation/dispatch";
import type { OutcomeLineRow, UrgentItemRow } from "../src/moderation/repo";

/**
 * The dispatch job's rules that need no database (3c design, sections 5, 7.8 and 7.12): which unanswered item of the
 * urgent lane still calls for someone, what each field of a daily update's line says, and how the job is started. The
 * rounds themselves run against the database in test/integration/moderation-dispatch.test.ts.
 */

const config = { APP_ORIGIN: "http://localhost:8081" } as CreateModerationOptions["config"];

describe("which unanswered item of the urgent lane still calls for someone", () => {
  const item = (over: Partial<UrgentItemRow> = {}): UrgentItemRow => ({
    caseId: "c",
    targetType: "post",
    targetId: "t",
    suspect: false,
    arrivedMs: 1_000,
    interimAfter: false,
    noteAfter: false,
    declinedAfter: false,
    newestDeclinedMs: null,
    postHidden: false,
    ...over,
  });
  const served = (newestServedAt: number | null = 500) => ({ served: 1, newestServedAt: newestServedAt === null ? null : new Date(newestServedAt) });
  const none = { served: 0, newestServedAt: null };

  test("a suspect item whose case reaches a served image: only a recorded choice not to seal ends it, and only for the images of posts created before it", () => {
    const suspect = (over: Partial<UrgentItemRow> = {}) => item({ suspect: true, ...over });
    expect(stillCalls(suspect(), served())).toBe(true);
    // Not a note, not a decision taken while deciding: some reader is still served the images.
    expect(stillCalls(suspect({ noteAfter: true, interimAfter: true }), served())).toBe(true);
    expect(stillCalls(suspect({ declinedAfter: true, newestDeclinedMs: 2_000 }), served(1_500))).toBe(false);
    // A post with a served image created after the newest recorded choice starts it again,
    expect(stillCalls(suspect({ declinedAfter: true, newestDeclinedMs: 2_000 }), served(2_001))).toBe(true);
    // also one created in the same millisecond: the alert errs on the side of repeating.
    expect(stillCalls(suspect({ declinedAfter: true, newestDeclinedMs: 2_000 }), served(2_000))).toBe(true);
    // A choice recorded before the item arrived says nothing about the item.
    expect(stillCalls(suspect({ declinedAfter: false, newestDeclinedMs: 900 }), served(100))).toBe(true);
    // What the case reaches must have been read for a suspect item.
    expect(() => stillCalls(suspect(), null)).toThrow();
  });

  test("a suspect item whose case reaches no served image: a decision taken while deciding, a note or a recorded choice not to seal after it arrived ends it", () => {
    const suspect = (over: Partial<UrgentItemRow> = {}) => item({ suspect: true, ...over });
    expect(stillCalls(suspect(), none)).toBe(true);
    expect(stillCalls(suspect({ interimAfter: true }), none)).toBe(false);
    expect(stillCalls(suspect({ noteAfter: true }), none)).toBe(false);
    expect(stillCalls(suspect({ declinedAfter: true, newestDeclinedMs: 2_000 }), none)).toBe(false);
  });

  test("any other item: a decision taken while deciding ends it; a note does only when the case is about an account or its post is not visible", () => {
    expect(stillCalls(item(), null)).toBe(true);
    expect(stillCalls(item({ interimAfter: true }), null)).toBe(false);
    // On a visible post a note never ends it.
    expect(stillCalls(item({ noteAfter: true }), null)).toBe(true);
    expect(stillCalls(item({ noteAfter: true, postHidden: true }), null)).toBe(false);
    expect(stillCalls(item({ noteAfter: true, targetType: "account" }), null)).toBe(false);
    // A recorded choice not to seal is about images: it says nothing about a threat.
    expect(stillCalls(item({ declinedAfter: true, newestDeclinedMs: 2_000, postHidden: true }), null)).toBe(true);
  });
});

describe("the module's background work", () => {
  afterEach(() => {

  /** The module over stand-ins that fail the test when a round touches them, and a lock that only records what it is asked. */
  function world(acquire: boolean, retention: "on" | "off" = "off") {
    const asked: { key: string; ttlMs: number }[] = [];
    const lock: JobLock = {
      acquire: async (key, _token, ttlMs) => {
        asked.push({ key, ttlMs });
        return acquire;
      },
      refresh: async () => undefined,
      release: async () => undefined,
    };
    const untouched = new Proxy({}, { get: () => () => Promise.reject(new Error("a round ran")) });
    const moderation = createModeration({
      apiDb: untouched as CreateModerationOptions["apiDb"],
      auth: untouched as CreateModerationOptions["auth"],
      social: untouched as CreateModerationOptions["social"],
      media: untouched as CreateModerationOptions["media"],
      rateLimitStore: new MemoryStore(),
      config: { ...config, MODERATION_RETENTION: retention } as CreateModerationOptions["config"],
      logger: pino({ level: "silent" }),
    });
    /** What the lock was asked for one job. */
    const of = (job: string) => asked.filter((entry) => entry.key === `job:${job}`);
    return { moderation, lock, asked, of };
  }

  test("startJobs runs the dispatch job under its own lock every ten minutes, from the end of the round before, until it is stopped", async () => {
    vi.useFakeTimers();
    // Another instance holds the lock: this one asks for it at every turn and runs no round.
    const w = world(false);
    const stop = w.moderation.startJobs(w.lock);
    expect([DISPATCH_JOB, DISPATCH_INTERVAL_MS]).toEqual(["moderation-dispatch", 10 * 60_000]);
    // The first round comes ten minutes after the start, not at once.
    await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(DISPATCH_INTERVAL_MS - 1);
    expect(w.of(DISPATCH_JOB)).toEqual([]);
    await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(1);
    expect(w.of(DISPATCH_JOB)).toEqual([{ key: "job:moderation-dispatch", ttlMs: DISPATCH_INTERVAL_MS }]);
    await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(DISPATCH_INTERVAL_MS);
    expect(w.of(DISPATCH_JOB)).toHaveLength(2);
    stop();
    const asked = w.asked.length;
    await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(3 * DISPATCH_INTERVAL_MS);
    expect(w.asked).toHaveLength(asked);
  });

  test("3f: startJobs runs the alert tick under its own lock every 30 seconds, also while retention is off, and stops it with the rest", async () => {
    vi.useFakeTimers();
    expect([ALERT_TICK_JOB, ALERT_TICK_INTERVAL_MS]).toEqual(["alert-tick", 30_000]);
    for (const retention of ["off", "on"] as const) {
      const w = world(false, retention);
      const stop = w.moderation.startJobs(w.lock);
      await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(ALERT_TICK_INTERVAL_MS - 1);
      expect(w.of(ALERT_TICK_JOB), retention).toEqual([]);
      await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(1);
      expect(w.of(ALERT_TICK_JOB), retention).toEqual([{ key: "job:alert-tick", ttlMs: ALERT_TICK_INTERVAL_MS }]);
      await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(ALERT_TICK_INTERVAL_MS);
      expect(w.of(ALERT_TICK_JOB), retention).toHaveLength(2);
      stop();
      await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(10 * ALERT_TICK_INTERVAL_MS);
      expect(w.of(ALERT_TICK_JOB), retention).toHaveLength(2);
    }
  });

  test("the queue-age alert has a key and a window of its own: once a day", () => {
    expect([WAITING_ALERT_KEY, WAITING_ALERT_WINDOW_MS]).toEqual(["moderation-waiting", 24 * 60 * 60_000]);
  });
});
```
